correct_text:
Thus, in order to support both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3, the cipher suites
   part of the "hello-params-grouping" grouping should include the
   following three parameters for configuring its permitted TLS
   algorithms: TLS Cipher Suites, TLS SignatureScheme, and TLS Supported
   Groups. Only TLS Cipher Suites is supported in this version.
notes:
The current text in RFC 9645 describes that the hello-params-grouping includes three parameters: TLS Cipher Suites, 
TLS SignatureScheme, and TLS Supported Groups. However, the YANG definition of hello-params-grouping does not 
include all of these parameters. In particular, only TLS Cipher Suites are currently represented.

As a result, the text cannot be realised by implementations using the published YANG model. This has been observed 
in practice when attempting to configure TLS 1.3 PSK‑DHE (psk_dhe_ke), where control over supported groups (e.g., named 
groups such as P‑256) is required but not expressible through the existing model.

Because modules such as ietf-system-tacacs-plus reuse hello-params-grouping, this limitation propagates to dependent models 
and prevents operators from configuring TLS parameters that are required for interoperability and policy enforcement.

This erratum clarifies the specification by updating the descriptive text to match the actual contents of the YANG grouping, thereby 
avoiding ambiguity for implementers and readers.

Verifier Notes:

My observation:

The discrepancy you have identified is real. The prose in Section 2 states that hello-params-grouping "should include the following three parameters for configuring its permitted TLS algorithms: TLS Cipher Suites, TLS SignatureScheme, and TLS Supported Groups," while the normative YANG definition in ietf-tls-common defines only two containers — tls-versions and cipher-suites. There are no data nodes for SignatureScheme or Supported Groups.

My intended Disposition: Hold for Document Update

I cannot mark this errata Verified, for two reasons.

First, the proposed correction is self-contradictory. Appending "Only TLS Cipher Suites is supported in this version" leaves the original sentence intact, which still asserts the grouping should include three parameters. 

Second, and more fundamentally, the errata mechanism cannot fix the underlying problem. If the original intent was for hello-params-grouping to expose all three TLS algorithm parameter categories — which the prose implies, and which would be necessary for complete TLS 1.3 negotiation control — the correct remedy is to add the missing YANG data nodes (signature-algorithms and supported-groups) to ietf-tls-common. That is a normative change to the data model and must go through the normal document update process. Errata cannot add YANG nodes to a published RFC.

The question for the authors and WG before I finalise the disposition I would like clarification on the original intent, as it determines the appropriate follow-on action:

Was the omission unintentional? If hello-params-grouping was always meant to include nodes for SignatureScheme and Supported Groups but they were inadvertently omitted, the right path is a document update that adds those nodes and makes the prose accurate.

Was the scope intentionally limited to cipher suites? If so, the prose needs to be revised more substantially — not just have a disclaimer appended — to remove the misleading "should include three parameters" framing.

Either way, I note that the absence of these nodes has real operational consequences: operators cannot use this module to constrain signature algorithms or named groups, limiting their ability to enforce TLS 1.3 policies in deployments such as TACACS+ over TLS. The WG should consider whether a document update is warranted regardless of which answer applies above. The authors might consider the VELOCE process to make this change :-)

Please respond within two weeks. Absent guidance from the authors or WG, I will mark the errata Hold for Document Update so that it is tracked and any future revision of RFC 9645 addresses it.
